source.name: MITRE D3FEND
source.note: The plain-language texts (short, simple, analogy and the Ukrainian names) are CyberPlain’s adaptation (CC BY 4.0). IDs, English names, definitions and hierarchy come from MITRE D3FEND (data/mitre/d3fend.json).

intro.title: A map of how to defend.
intro.lead: MITRE D3FEND is an open catalog of defensive measures. It is maintained by the nonprofit MITRE, the same organization behind ATT&CK.
intro.body: The catalog describes not products but defensive actions: what exactly you need to do so an attack fails or gets noticed. The same measure can appear in different products, and one product usually performs several measures.

terms.title: Why.
terms.text: The goal of defense: know your systems, harden them, spot an attack, contain it, deceive, evict, recover.

terms.title: With what.
terms.text: A group of similar measures within a tactic, for example “Agent Authentication” or “Network Traffic Analysis.”

terms.title: How exactly.
terms.text: A specific defensive measure with its own ID. Techniques can have even more specific variants.

intro.sectionLead: Seven tactics — from “know what you’re protecting” to “put everything back the way it was.” Click a tactic to see its categories and techniques.
intro.caveat: This is a catalog, not a checklist. No company does everything, and no product covers everything: what matters is which measures protect against your own risks.
